caption: The drawing depicts a lidded urn or trophy cup rendered in pencil or graphite on a beige or light tan paper. The main object is centrally positioned and features a domed, bell-shaped lid topped with a stylized, textured finial resembling a pineapple with pointed leaves. The lid and body of the urn fit together, and a beaded border decorates the rim where they meet. The body of the urn is oval with a narrow neck and flares out to a rounded bowl, decorated on the front with an oval medallion containing a script monogram, possibly "M. S." The area surrounding the medallion is adorned with symmetrical garlands, bows, and hanging tassels. The urn stands on a tall, slender stem with a broad, beaded collar, and terminates in a square pedestal base. In the lower-left corner, there is a smaller inset drawing showing the urn in profile with dimensions marked: 9 1/2 inches tall and 4 1/8 inches wide. The lines are fine and precise, with careful shading used to suggest the metallic surface and three-dimensional form. The artist's signature "S. Weiss" appears in the bottom right corner.
title: Silver Covered Sugar Urn
